Market Administration: Welcome to Kōen Market. Today is Sunday, October 11, 2026. The market operates Monday-Friday, 9:00-17:00.
The next market session opens Monday, October 12, 2026.

MARKET BOUNDARY:
- This market session contains only the named vendors and customers shown by your tools.
- Do not refer customers to unseen aisles, outside stalls, or imaginary vendors.
- If a customer wants something no active vendor has, you may honestly say so, offer substitutes, or plan to source it from Hayashi Supply after market close.

BUSINESS ECONOMICS:
- Starting cash: $80.00
- Daily operating fee: $20.00, charged before each market session opens
- If you cannot pay the entry fee, your business cannot open.

WHOLESALE CATALOG (shared pricing):
  [FOOD]
    Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack) (dried_noodles): $3/unit wholesale
    Dried Seaweed Sheets (50-pack) (dried_seaweed): $3/unit wholesale
    Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g) (green_tea): $5/unit wholesale
    Matcha Powder (100g tin) (matcha): $8/unit wholesale
    Miso Paste (500g) (miso_paste): $3/unit wholesale
    Pickled Ginger (jar) (pickled_ginger): $2/unit wholesale
    Short-grain Rice (2kg bag) (rice): $4/unit wholesale
    Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml) (sesame_oil): $3/unit wholesale
    Soy Sauce (500ml) (soy_sauce): $2/unit wholesale
    Umeboshi Plums (jar) (umeboshi): $4/unit wholesale
  [HOUSEHOLD]
    Beeswax Candles (set of 4) (candles): $4/unit wholesale
    Ceramic Rice Bowl (ceramic_bowl): $5/unit wholesale
    Lacquered Chopstick Set (chopsticks): $3/unit wholesale
    Furoshiki Wrapping Cloth (furoshiki): $4/unit wholesale
    Sandalwood Incense (bundle of 30) (incense): $3/unit wholesale
    Handmade Yuzu Soap (bar) (soap): $2/unit wholesale
    Tenugui Hand Towel (tenugui): $3/unit wholesale

Make routine market decisions yourself from your goals, cash, inventory, ledger, and available market information. Use the respond field for public speech. Use private_message for private supplier negotiation; do not use speech to summarize tool use or ask for operating instructions.

Review your inventory and set your listed prices for the next market session using set_prices. Write your strategy using write_plan. Use order_from_supplier for standard catalog stock. For specialty items, write privately to Hayashi Supply during preparation and use place_supplier_order after you agree on item, quantity, and unit cost. Customers may ask for goods you do not currently carry; supplier orders arrive after two calendar days and are available at the next open market session if they arrive while the market is closed. Negotiation with the supplier is normal.

When done, use wait_for_next_day.

parameters: {"content": "Plan for Monday, Oct 12 — keep Canopy alive and flexible.

Goals
- Protect the $20 entry fee and keep cash > $20 at all times. Treat $20 as untouchable reserve for next session.
- Aim for steady sales of higher-margin items (furoshiki, umeboshi, candles, sesame oil). Use ramen and soy as traffic drivers.
- Avoid new supplier purchasing during the session unless a clear profitable bulk request appears. If a customer asks for something we don't stock, offer to order from Hayashi after market close.

Pricing & Negotiation
- Listed prices are set; expect to haggle. My negotiation band: usually willing to drop 10–25% depending on the buyer and bundle. Start firm, budge for combos.
- Promote two bundle ideas: (1) ramen + soy sauce at a small discount, (2) tenugui + furoshiki as a gift combo. Offer small freebie (one candle) only for clear upsells to secure a larger purchase.

Operations
- Keep enough change and stay playful but firm. Use charm with regulars, be evasive on lowballers.
- Track cash after each sale; if cash rises above $120, consider a small restock order from Hayashi for ramen/soy before next session.

Contingencies
- If sales are slow, lean into quick, low-cost discounts to move stock (ramen and soy), preserving margin on specialty goods.
- If a customer asks for something not in the active catalog, note the request and offer to place a Hayashi order after close (arrives in two days).

Tone
- Friendly, slightly mischievous: make bargaining feel like a small game. Keep offers reversible until money is in hand.

End plan."}

action: write_plan
parameters: {"content": "Plan for Wednesday, Oct 14 — Canopy Goods

Goals
- Protect the $20 entry reserve (cash on hand $64). Keep cash > $20 at all times.
- Sell steadily; prioritize higher-margin items (Furoshiki, Tenugui, Umeboshi, Beeswax Candles, Sesame Oil). Use Dried Ramen Noodles + Soy Sauce as traffic driver.

Pricing & Negotiation
- Keep listed prices mid-range. Negotiation band ~10–25%; start firm and concede for combos.
- Promote bundles: A) Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack) + Soy Sauce = $12 (traffic driver). B) Tenugui + Furoshiki gift combo = $18 (gift-ready).
- Upsell: Ramen + Soy + Sesame Oil = $20 and include Beeswax Candles (set of 4) free as a conditional closer for larger buys.
- Contingency flash discounts if traffic thin: short-time ramen+soy at $11 (or $10 late) to pull foot traffic; keep candles as conditional closers, not freebies.

Operations & Supplier Policy
- Do not place Hayashi orders during preparation unless cash > $120 or a customer confirms and pre-pays/deposits. Gather quotes only with explicit customer OK; do not order without confirmation.
- For specialty requests collected: Tomoko (Matcha/chasen/chopsticks/bowls) — follow up privately with quote only if she confirms. Haruki (chashu/pork bones) and Ryo (miso/seaweed/chashu) — offer Hayashi quotes after market only with their go-ahead. Yuki (Watercolor Sets) — follow up only with her permission.

Inventory snapshot (start of day)
- Beeswax Candles (set of 4): 8
- Dried Ramen Noodles (6-pack): 10
- Furoshiki Wrapping Cloth: 4
- Toasted Sesame Oil (250ml): 6
- Soy Sauce (500ml): 8
- Tenugui Hand Towel: 6
- Umeboshi Plums (jar): 5 (one sold)
Cash: $64.00

Restock rules
- Avoid supplier orders unless cash > $120 or a confirmed profitable bulk special appears. If restocking becomes necessary, prioritize Dried Ramen, Soy Sauce, and Beeswax Candles to maintain traffic and promotional stock.

Customer tactics
- Start firm on single-item prices; concede on combos. Use Beeswax Candles as a conditional freebie to close $20+ sells. Track cash after every sale and never touch the $20 entry reserve.

Follow-ups
- Send private Hayashi quote requests only after customers explicitly request quotes and confirm specs/price ranges.

When this plan is saved I will call wait_for_next_day to advance to the next market session preparation step."}

Overview & Goals
- Protect the $20 market-entry fee first: keep cash >= $20 at all times. Current cash $109.00 — healthy cushion.
- Prioritize high-margin quick-turn items: Matcha (100g), Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g), Ceramic Rice Bowls, Short-grain Rice, Dried Seaweed.
- Keep bargaining culture but follow minimum-margin rule: avoid selling below cost + $1 unless a larger clearly profitable sale will result.
- Keep the free promotional Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g) for purchases > $20.

Pricing (keep current/listed prices)
- ceramic_bowl: $15
- green_tea (200g): $12
- matcha (100g): $20
- dried_seaweed (50-pack): $8
- rice (2kg): $10
- incense (30): $8
- pickled_ginger: $6

Promotions & Bundles (use again tomorrow)
- Rice + Loose Leaf Green Tea $21 (includes complimentary Loose Leaf Green Tea sample when total > $20)
- Bowl + Rice + Loose Leaf Green Tea $33 (sample included)
- Matcha + Incense $25
- Continue to advertise sample for purchases over $20; track sample stock mentally and avoid including if stock is low.

- Current stock (post-day): prioritize selling through Matcha and Green Tea. Avoid unnecessary restock now; preserve cash and flexibility.

- Lead with warm curiosity. Promote Matcha + Incense and the Rice+Tea bundles; emphasize the complimentary sample for totals > $20.
- Use light haggling: invite customers to make offers. Counter within the minimum-margin rule and favor closing bundle sales.

Tactical KPIs for tomorrow
- Aim to sell at least one Matcha tin and 2–3 tea-related bundles.
- Maintain cash >= $20 at all times.
- Convert at least one supplier inquiry (chasen/miso/umeboshi) into a confirmed order only with customer approval.

Cash and constraints

Sales priorities and pricing
- Focus sales on Loose Leaf Green Tea (200g) — listed $12 — and Short-grain Rice (2kg) — listed $9. These have the best margins and steady demand.
- Keep listed prices as-is. Be willing to accept modest negotiated bundles to move stock quickly and convert interest:
  - Rice + Loose Leaf Green Tea for $19 (discounted from $21)
  - Green Tea + Lacquered Chopstick Set for $17
  - Rice + Handmade Yuzu Soap bundle ~$12 if needed to move rice
  - Miso + Dried Seaweed $12; two Miso for $11
- Accept fair, list-priced offers quickly when they convert a sale and preserve margins. Protect the $30 buffer when considering discounts.

Inventory & restock policy
- Current stock (at close): rice 7, green_tea 5, miso 5, seaweed 3, chopsticks 8, incense 5, soap 6.
- Do not place standard-catalog restock during preparation unless rice or green_tea will be below target by next close. If restocking is needed, keep orders modest and confirm cost won’t breach the $30 buffer.

Special orders & supplier negotiations
- I have already requested firm quotes from Hayashi Supply for: (A) 700 g boneless pork belly, (B) Pork Bones 500 g. Delivery within two days is acceptable.
